runtimeArchitecture: self-contained procedural WebGL2 raster workbench loaded from a deterministic gzip payload

easyRain.creator: William Faucher
easyRain.adoption: Publicly documented capability organization and visual-quality targets were distilled. No EasyRain commercial Blueprint, Niagara graph, material graph, texture, flipbook, model, audio or binary asset was copied.

brickMother.adoption: Historical fired-clay proportions, seeded form hierarchy, roughness, porosity, wet-darkening and runoff behavior were independently adapted into the Rain test wall.

tilesMother.adoption: V0.5 pan-tile and cover-tile cross-section equations, independent thickness, hand-form variation, laps, channels and eave drainage direction were independently adapted into the Rain roof specimen.

distilledRainRules: falling precipitation state remains separate from persistent surface-water state
visible streak length derives from terminal velocity and shutter duration
near, middle and distant rain use distinct spatial-frequency and opacity budgets
rain glimmer depends on light-view alignment and background contrast
roof shelter suppresses rain beneath solid cover
pan-tile channels and cover-tile seams guide runoff toward the eave
fired clay absorbs water, darkens progressively and retains moisture longer than glazed or metallic surfaces
puddles, ripples, eave drips and surface wetness read the same rain-flux clock
implementedFeatures: programmatic pan and cover roof tiles
knownLimits: This is an independent visual simulation and not the EasyRain commercial implementation.
The public EasyRain tutorial has been located and capability-level facts have been extracted; undocumented commercial graph internals remain unknown.
The current renderer is a bounded inspection scene rather than a large-world precipitation streamer.
Audio, thunder and live meteorological data are outside this Rain candidate.
Native user-hardware 2K and 4K performance remains unverified.
